The new agreement would begin later in 2026 as territory rights become available, before being fully in effect in early 2029. == Reception == === Box office === {{As of|2026|8|3|df=US}}, ''Spider-Man: Brand New Day'' has grossed $407 million in the United States and Canada, and $646 million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $1.053 billion, making it the [[2026 in film#Highest-grossing films|second-highest-grossing film of 2026]].{{Cite web |title=2026 Top-Grossing Worldwide Movies |url=https://www.the-numbers.com/box-office-records/worldwide/all-movies/cumulative/released-in-2026 |access-date=2026-08-04 |website=[[The Numbers (website)|The Numbers]]}} Its $927 million opening weekend was the [[List of highest-grossing openings for films#Biggest worldwide openings on record|second-best of all time]] behind ''[[Avengers: Endgame#United States and Canada|Avengers: Endgame]]'' (2019). On Monday, August 3, ''Brand New Day'' became the [[List of fastest-grossing films#Fastest to $1 billion|second-fastest film]] to gross $1 billion, doing so in six days. In the United States and Canada, the film grossed $72 million from its Wednesday and Thursday preview screenings, surpassing the record previously held by ''Endgame''. It went on to gross $169.8 million for its opening day, which included the preview screenings, which also surpassed ''Endgame''{{'s}} record of $157.4 million. ''Brand New Day''{{'s}} Saturday gross of $101.5 million was second best all-time to ''Endgame'' ($109.2 million), leading to an opening weekend of $360 million. This was the [[List of highest-grossing openings for films#Biggest openings in the United States and Canada|highest opening weekend gross in the territory]], surpassing ''Endgame'' ($357.1 million). Pre-release estimates had the film grossing $260–280 million in its opening weekend, with Sony estimating a $195 million opening. On its fourth day of release, it generated the highest Monday gross of any film with $47 million, surpassing ''[[Black Panther (film)|Black Panther]]''{{'s}} $40 million in 2018. Outside of the United States and Canada, the film grossed $573 million its opening weekend, surpassing the pre-release estimates of $275–300 million. In France, it opened on July 29, 2026 in 978 theaters and drew 650,130 viewers on its opening day, making it the best opening day for a film at the French box office since ''Endgame''. In India, the film grossed {{Currency|10000000|USD}} in two days, surpassing ''Endgame'' to become the best opening ever for a Hollywood film in India.{{Cite web |last=Mathur |first=Abhimanyu |date=August 1, 2026 |title=Spider-Man Brand New Day India box office: Tom Holland film crosses ₹100 crore in 2 days; outpaces Dhurandhar, Avengers |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/entertainment/hollywood/spider-man-brand-new-day-india-box-office-collection-tom-holland-film-100-crore-in-2-days-outpaces-dhurandhar-avengers-101785554325934.html |access-date=August 1, 2026 |website=[[Hindustan Times]]}} ==== Pre-sale ticket records ==== ''Brand New Day'' had the best first-day ticket pre-sales in the United States in five years since ''No Way Home'' in 2021, which had an estimated $78 million in pre-sales. This was later revised to $100 million, with Dolby Cinema also seeing record pre-sales, having nearly two-thirds of available tickets sold. === Critical response === {{Multiple image | total_width = 300 | align = right | image1 = TomHolland-byPhilipRomano.jpg | image2 = Destin Daniel Cretton by Gage Skidmore.jpg | footer = [[Tom Holland]] (''left'') and [[Destin Daniel Cretton]] (''right'') were generally praised by critics for their performance and direction, respectively. }} On the [[review aggregator]] website [[Rotten Tomatoes]], 90% based on 372 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 7.7/10. The website's consensus reads: "Spinning a web of spectacular set pieces together with mature emotional stakes and Tom Holland's soulful performance, ''Brand New Day'' is a promising reset that portends Spidey will remain sticky on the big screen for years to come."{{Cite Rotten Tomatoes |id=spider_man_brand_new_day |type=m |title=Spider-Man: Brand New Day |access-date=August 4, 2026}}{{cbignore}} [[Metacritic]], which uses a [[weighted average]], assigned the film a score of 66 out of 100 based on 56 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.{{Cite Metacritic |id=spider-man-brand-new-day |type=movie |title=Spider-Man: Brand New Day |access-date=August 1, 2026}}{{cbignore}} Audiences polled by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film an average grade of "A" on an A+ to F scale, while 88% of those surveyed by [[PostTrak]] said they would definitely recommend the film. Pete Hammond for ''[[Deadline Hollywood]]'' called ''Brand New Day'' a "dark and thrilling new chapter" for the franchise, praising [[Tom Holland]]'s performance, [[Destin Daniel Cretton]]'s direction, and the film's balance of character drama and superhero action. [[Owen Gleiberman]] for ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' praised the film for its action, villain, and Holland's performance, but described the film as "arduous", "clunkily episodic", and "half an hour too long", arguing that it is more self-serious than emotionally involving. [[Peter Bradshaw]] for ''[[The Guardian]]'' praised the ambitious tone, strong performances and emotional focus, particularly highlighting [[Zendaya]] and Holland's chemistry. However, he found the film uneven, with some familiar superhero elements limiting its impact. William Bibbiani for ''[[TheWrap]]'' praised ''Brand New Day'' as "a fantastic film about Peter Parker" and "one of the highlights of the whole franchise", commending its emotional, character-driven story and the performances of Holland and [[Jon Bernthal]], despite criticizing the villain's plan as illogical. John Nugent for ''[[Empire (magazine)|Empire]]'' gave the film four out of five stars, praising its grounded, comic-faithful approach and Holland's performance, describing Spider-Man as "still Marvel's ace in the pack", while noting that the second half loses momentum due to unnecessary ties to the wider [[Marvel Cinematic Universe]] (MCU). David Rooney of ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'' praised Cretton's direction for balancing "adrenaline and feeling", while highlighting "the humanity that has always been Spidey's greatest strength", Holland's "never-better" performance, and the film's emotional focus on Peter, though he criticized occasional pacing issues and plot convolutions. [[David Ehrlich]] for ''[[IndieWire]]'' gave the film a C−, describing it as a "dull and downbeat action sequel" that "causes more problems than it cures", criticizing its pacing, its reliance on MCU setup, and its failure to meaningfully advance Peter's story, although he praised Holland's performance and considered Cretton "a more sure-footed stylist" than [[Jon Watts]]. David Fear for ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' criticized the film for relying too heavily on fan service, MCU crossovers and franchise setup at the expense of Spider-Man's story, arguing that Peter risks becoming "a supporting player in his own movie", while praising Holland's performance and the emotional scenes between Peter and MJ. == Future == Pascal stated in November 2021 that ''Brand New Day'' was planned to be the first film in a new ''Spider-Man'' trilogy. In early 2026, Holland revisited his previous comments about not wanting to play Spider-Man past the age of 30 and hoping to pass the mantle to another actor. Since the latter had not yet happened by his 30th birthday, Holland said he may need to "change the quote to 37" and added that "playing Spider-Man has been the joy of my life... I'll do it for as long as they'll have me." In July, Pascal expressed the hope that Cretton would continue to direct ''Spider-Man'' films in the future. Feige also noted how the live-action ''Spider-Man'' films had a "destiny" to introduce Miles Morales following the conclusion of the [[Spider-Verse (franchise)|''Spider-Verse'' film trilogy]] with ''Beyond the Spider-Verse'', and that he and Pascal have had "in-depth" discussions about what the next five additional ''Spider-Man'' films could be about. Holland said a plan had been in place since the end of ''No Way Home'' regarding another actor succeeding him as Spider-Man and that he has a "really clear vision" about passing the role to another Spider-Man: Brand New Day is a 2026 American superhero film based on the Marvel Comics character Spider-Man. Produced by Columbia Pictures, Marvel Studios, and Pascal Pictures, and distributed by Sony Pictures Releasing, it is the 38th film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) and the fourth film in the MCU Spider-Man film series following Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021). The film was directed by Destin Daniel Cretton, and written by Chris McKenna and Erik Sommers. Tom Holland stars as Peter Parker / Spider-Man, alongside Zendaya, Sadie Sink, Jacob Batalon, Jon Bernthal, Florence Pugh, Tramell Tillman, Marisa Tomei, and Mark Ruffalo. In the film, Peter anonymously protects New York City as the hero Spider-Man and investigates a powerful new threat while his superpowers undergo a surprising and potentially dangerous evolution.
Sony was developing a fourth MCU Spider-Man film by August 2019, and producer Amy Pascal revealed in November 2021 that it was intended to be the first in a new trilogy starring Holland. Work on the story began that December, with Holland more involved in development than he was for the previous films. McKenna and Sommers returned as writers by February 2023, Cretton was hired to direct by October 2024, and the title—derived from the 2008 comic book storyline "Brand New Day" that reset Spider-Man's status quo—was announced in March 2025. The producers wanted Holland's Peter to be a "proper Spider-Man" for the first time, on his own and fighting street-level crime in New York City. Ahead of filming, Bernthal and Ruffalo were revealed to be reprising their MCU roles of Frank Castle / Punisher and Bruce Banner / Hulk. Filming took place from August to December 2025, with location filming in Glasgow, Scotland, and throughout England. Soundstage work occurred at Pinewood Studios in England.
Spider-Man: Brand New Day premiered at the Dolby Theatre in Hollywood, Los Angeles, on July 27, 2026, and was released in the United States on July 31, as part of Phase Six of the MCU. The film received generally positive reviews from critics and has grossed $1.053 billion worldwide, becoming the third-highest-grossing Spider-Man film and the second-highest-grossing film of 2026. It also had the highest opening weekend gross of all time in the United States and Canada and the second-highest worldwide.
